observations: What I read: the whole prepared request (base.decisions, dialoguePolicy, dialogueInstructions and base.script with all 23 panels 01-1..06-4), all of works/auto-6294ee8a2094/source/original.txt, all of works/auto-6294ee8a2094/workflow/source-coverage.json, all of docs/REVISION-AND-REVIEWS.md, and AGENTS.md as supplied in the project instructions. In docs/PROMPTS.md I only searched for script/dialogueReview/reviewer lines; I did not read it in full. I also read the previous response script-all-r6.json for context. Every file was readable. No artwork exists at the script stage, so I inspected no images and certify nothing visual. A note on reading order: the source and the request were loaded in the same step. I then read only the lettered dialogue/caption fields in panel order before comparing them with the source.

The r6 issue is fixed, and I checked it myself. Panel 05-4 now has "section": "departure". That section's location ('Clinic entrance from the street side, morning sun') and its Ravi-only costume match the 05-4 scene: Ravi steps outside, waves back with his right hand and holds his phone in his left. The indoor 'reception' data (monitor, waiting chairs, Ananya/Meera costumes) no longer goes to this panel. Every defined section is now used at least once: clinic-morning, onboarding, reception, consultation, departure, travel, vision and closing.

Reading the lettering alone, it holds together. 'the rest' (01-3) points back to Meera's list (01-2). 'here' (02-2) refers to the laptop in 02-1. 'And our team...' (02-3) follows straight on from Ananya. Each question is answered in the next panel: 03-1 to 03-2, 03-2 to 03-3, 04-1 to 04-2 and 05-2 to 05-3. 'your concerns' (04-4) refers back to 04-2. All lines and captions match the source word for word. The only split is 01-2, where one Meera line becomes two balloons by the same speaker, with nobody speaking in between. No turns are merged across another speaker. The voices fit: Ananya calm and decisive, Meera polite and helpful, Ravi casual and warm.

Product roles and vision separation follow the source. Practice is on the clinic laptop (02-1), Care on the staff phone (02-3) and Health on Ravi's own phone (05-1, 05-2). Only 06-2 and 06-3 carry 'WELBUK VISION' and the pale-blue vignette. 06-1 keeps the conditional 'may' and uses the non-vision 'travel' section. 06-4 returns to the present with no vignette. Screens show only abstract blocks and icons, and 03-3 rules out ID cards and written papers. I found no diagnosis, treatment advice, real data or invented feature. The stethoscope stays a worn costume item ('not in use').

Props and hands are consistent. Ravi's bag goes strap-held (03-1, 03-4), to the floor (04-1, 04-4), then back on his shoulder (05-1, 05-4). His phone goes pocket, right hand (05-1), both hands (05-2), left hand (05-4), lap (06-1). Meera's staff phone stays in her right hand in 02-3, 02-4 and 06-4. No hand is given two tasks at once. Screen direction holds within each scene: Ravi left / Meera right on page 3, Ananya left / Ravi right across 04-1..04-4, Meera left / Ravi right across 05-1..05-3. The off-panel gaze directions in 03-2, 04-2, 04-3, 05-2 and 05-3 match.

Not blocking, for later stages: (a) The Meera/Ravi sides flip between page 3 and page 5. Page 4 comes between them and 05-1 is a fresh corner shot, so this is acceptable, but the storyboard review should confirm it reads naturally. (b) heldBy lists only one hand for two-handed grips (05-2 ravi-phone 'ravi.right', 06-3 family-tablet 'partner.left'); the hands fields make the grip clear. (c) 02-3 production.before says Ananya handed Meera the phone, but the prop's before value is 'on the desk'. This is a small wording mismatch with no effect on the art.

No artwork, storyboard or lettering exists for this request. Nothing visual is certified. Face identity, hands, readable-text absence and vision styling must be checked on the real images in later stages.

panels.observation: The source caption 'A busy day at Dr. Ananya's clinic.' is kept word for word. It names Ananya and sets up the 'busy' premise that Meera's complaint in 01-2 depends on.
Meera's single source line is split at the ellipsis into two consecutive balloons by the same speaker, with nothing in between. The list gives 'everything' its referent.
Ananya's line is word for word. 'the rest' depends on the paperwork list in 01-2, and her looking at the desk gives her reason to act, as in the source's 'looks thoughtfully at the reception desk'.
The onboarding caption is word for word, and evening light marks the time change. The Practice label names the source's 'laptop view of Welbuk Practice' and claims no feature.
The line is word for word. 'here' refers to the laptop setup in 02-1, and her considering team roles (from the source) leads into Meera's line.
'And our team...' is word for word and continues Ananya's 02-2 line directly with no other speaker between them. The Care label matches the source's 'staff phone displaying Welbuk Care'.
'One team. Better coordination.' is word for word and sums up 02-2 and 02-3. Meera's silent nod is a manga reaction, not a dropped line.
Ravi's greeting and request are word for word. 'I'd like to see the doctor' is what Meera's 'Of course' in 03-2 answers.
The line is word for word. It answers 03-1 and asks the consent question that 03-3 replies to, so consent comes before any data is entered, as the source requires.
'Yes, please.' answers the 03-2 consent question directly. Meera types into blank fields only, with no ID cards or papers, matching 'no actual identifying data'.
'You're all set, Ravi. Please have a seat.' is word for word. His name follows naturally from the registration, and the gesture to the chairs leads into page 4.
Ananya's greeting is word for word. 'Tell me what brings you in' is the question 04-2 answers, and the same costumes show it is the same visit after the place change.
'I've been feeling tired lately.' answers 04-1 word for word as the source's routine concern. No diagnosis or advice is written or drawn.
The caption is word for word. It is backed by a silent, attentive listener and the closed laptop, and it comments on the 04-1/04-2 exchange without adding medical content.
The line is word for word, and 'your concerns' refers back to 04-2. No instruments are in use and no treatment advice is given, as the source requires.
Meera's line is word for word and keeps the careful 'designed to help'. The return to reception places it after the consultation.

Ravi's question is word for word and depends on Meera's explanation in 05-1. The abstract calendar and heart cards stand in for the source's 'appointments and health information' without showing any data.
'That's the idea' answers the 05-2 question directly. 'what is available to you' is kept word for word, so no unlaunched feature is implied.

The caption is word for word, and Ravi leaving with his phone and bag shows the source's 'leaves, reassured'. The panel now uses the 'departure' section, so the outdoor scene and its section data agree.
The caption is word for word and keeps the conditional 'may'. The non-vision train-window panel carries the change of time and place without presenting the vision as current.
The 'WELBUK VISION' label the source asks for and the caption are word for word inside the vignette. The symbolic specialist and the dotted links do not suggest a launched referral feature.
The caption is word for word. The repeated vision label and the vignette keep the family wellness app clearly conceptual, with abstract icons only.
The three product labels and the final caption are word for word. The present-day group shot ties Practice, Care and Health back to Ananya (02-1), Meera (02-3) and Ravi (05-2).
